summary: @adminide-stack/utils ships appended eval(atob(...)) loader with Ethereum RPC interception payload
details: lib/index.js is a webpack bundle whose authored source (per the shipped source map) only re-exports a logger module. An extra line `eval(atob("<~50KB base64>"))` has been appended after the webpack footer and is not present in the authored sources. The decoded blob is heavily obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style string-array dispatcher (`_0x5c1d` with hex-named helpers and runtime array shuffling) and contains Ethereum JSON-RPC method strings (`eth_blockNumber`, `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `eth_getTransactionCount`), public Ethereum RPC provider hostnames (`*.publicnode.com`, `h.drpc.org`, `public.*.blockscout`), nonce/transaction handling, a browser User-Agent, and `node:http`/`https` POST plumbing. It sets `global.i='A10-npm_inject'` and hooks `module`/`require`/`process`. The payload executes at `require('@adminide-stack/utils')` time, so any consumer importing the package runs the attacker code. The combination of a post-build appended obfuscated loader, mismatch with the authored source map (a utility that only re-exports a logger), and Ethereum RPC interception strings matches the npm wallet-drainer supply-chain campaign and places any wallet/transaction-signing activity reachable from the host process at risk.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
